title: Should a standing answer ever expire?
context: Earlier answers past their expiry date are no longer suggested, yet a standing answer as described lasts forever, so an old choice could keep skipping a person after the situation has changed. Recommended: it lasts until someone removes it. That is what "always" says and what the rule shape in issue 822 holds. Each use prints a line naming the rule and is logged, and removing it is one command. A 90-day expiry would re-ask people who said always, and following the question type could end a rule within 1 to 90 days. The cost: a stale rule keeps answering until someone notices it.
